text:
Asha (Design): Heads-up: prototyping a compact validation pattern for the settings panel. Need quick feedback on inline vs summary balance and destructive confirmations. High-level goal: make errors obvious without noise on mobile. Ravi (Product): TL;DR: immediate inline hints for simple constraints, summary for multi-field/semantic errors. But let's avoid double-verbage where both show the same message. Diego (Eng): Agreed. Implementation idea: treat inline errors as contextual hints tied to the input; summary contains unique, cross-field or server-side issues. We can dedupe messages by ID to avoid repeating. Lina (Accessibility): Important: screen reader users need a single, predictable announcement pattern. I recommend: on submit failure -> focus summary (role=alert, aria-live=assertive) and include links to offending fields. Inline errors should use aria-live=polite so they don't interrupt typing. Molly (DevEx): Mobile density: asterisks crowd labels. Consider inline "(required)" on the first column in desktop, but for mobile collapse label into "Name\n(required)" stacked. Also propose a visual-only asterisk with aria-required on the control. Asha (Design): Copy synonyms debate: "Please fix 2 errors to continue" vs "We need a couple more things". I'm leaning toward the former for clarity. Also thinking about destructive flows: three-tier pattern — lightweight: inline undo (toast), medium: checkbox confirmation, high: typed-confirm. Thoughts? Ravi (Product): Three-tier seems right. For medium we should show what will be deleted and require a short explicit consent like "I understand this will affect X items" with a checkbox. For typed-confirm, show the exact resource name and a clear short line: "This action is permanent." Keep CTA wording consistent: "Delete" vs "Confirm Delete". Diego (Eng): Dev considerations: typed-confirm should be case-sensitive? Usually case-insensitive to avoid friction. But for highest risk, maybe exact match. We can param: allowExactMatch boolean. Also rate-limit attempts to avoid brute force. Lina (Accessibility): Typed-confirm guidance: avoid relying purely on visual masking. Announce instructions via offscreen text with role=note. Also ensure the input has aria-describedby pointing to the instruction. Molly (DevEx): Keyboard flows: cancel must be first focusable action after the typed-confirm, so keyboard users can back out without tabbing through destructive confirm. Also Esc should close and reset the typed input. Asha (Design): UX flow proposal for form validation: - On input blur: run lightweight validation, show inline hint (aria-live=polite). - On submit: run full validation, render error summary, focus summary, highlight inline fields. - If server returns cross-field error: put it in summary only with per-field anchors. Diego (Eng): Example error summary structure we can implement quickly: ```html

Please review the following issues:

  • Name is required
  • Retention must be between 1 and 365 days
``` Lina (Accessibility): That works. Ensure the in-page anchors also set focus to the input and expose the inline error via aria-describedby. Molly (DevEx): Small edge: when auto-scrolling to inline error on small screens, avoid hiding the call-to-action (Save) behind sticky headers. We might scroll so the input sits 48px below top. Ravi (Product): Copy for summary headline: proposal "There are 3 issues preventing save" vs "Please fix 3 issues to save". The latter ties to the action. I'm partial to "Please fix 3 issues to save." Asha (Design): I'll standardize on "Please fix X issues to save". For the per-field microcopy, use sentence case and keep examples short: e.g., "Enter a valid email address." Diego (Eng): Regarding dedupe: if a server returns both a per-field and summary message, we'll prefer the server message in summary and keep inline hint generic. Also add an error-code meta to aid instrumentation. ops-bot: Note: logging event proposal: validation.summary_shown, validation.inline_shown, destruct.typed_confirm_attempt. Add to events backlog. Molly (DevEx): Question about undo: For bulk deletes with inline undo, how long should the toast persist? 8-12s? Also provide a list view filter like "Show recently deleted" for 30 days? That's product scope but worth discussing. Ravi (Product): 10s toast + an "Undo" button seems reasonable. Long-term we can add soft-delete for 30 days as a separate feature. Lina (Accessibility): Toasts must be focusable and announced (aria-live polite) and not trap keyboard focus. Also ensure persistent undo is discoverable via keyboard and screen reader. Asha (Design): Actions: I'll push a Figma prototype demonstrating desktop/mobile label density, hybrid validation flow, and the three destructive confirm variants. Please review by Friday midday. Diego (Eng): I'll draft a small implementation doc with props: allowExactMatch, cooldownMs, summaryFocusBehavior. Molly (DevEx): I'll prepare a keyboard + a11y checklist and test cases. Ravi (Product): I'll own copy and risk-tier definitions. Asha (Design): Thanks team. Posting link to WIP Figma when ready. :sparkles:
